Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Do not add a greeting, subject, signature, conclusion, or fact that the input did not supply.", "input": "the access list for the shared studio at north annex has been updated for the spring booking period, and this note explains what changed and what did not. it is still the working list for the two rooms on the second floor, the print room and the recording room; it is not an attendance record, and a name on the list does not mean a person has booked either room. the list is kept by the studio coordinator, but the booking calendar is kept separately by the front desk. this matters because some people were looking at the access list to check whether a room was free, and that information is not there. the current copy is in the cabinet beside the second-floor stairs, with a read-only copy in the staff folder online.

for this update, the coordinator compared the existing names with the booking requests received by march 12 and with the staff records for current studio members. the comparison did not change anyone’s room booking, membership status, or key deposit. it was only used to decide who should remain on the access list for the spring period. the coordinator also checked each entry against the contact details that were already held, rather than asking members to send new personal information. where a record had an old email address, the list now shows the current one if it was already available in the staff record. it does not show phone numbers, emergency contacts, or the reason a person needs access.

1. changes to names and access

mara ellis and jon bell were added to the list because both have active memberships and submitted spring access requests. mara can use the print room on weekdays from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m.; jon can use the recording room on tuesdays and thursdays from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. their names are listed with those time limits, not as unrestricted access. priya shah remains listed for both rooms, with her existing weekday hours unchanged. she asked whether her saturday workshop booking could be added too, but that booking is on the calendar only and does not extend her regular access hours. the list still shows her weekday permission only.

eli turner’s entry was removed because his membership ended on february 28. this removal applies to both rooms and to the north annex entrance list managed by the studio; it does not change the separate loan record for a microphone he returned last month. the coordinator has not yet received a completed spring request from noa kim, so noa is not added in this update. if that request arrives, the coordinator will check it against the membership record before changing the list. until then, noa’s name is not on the current copy, even though an older printout remains in the equipment cupboard. the older printout is marked for replacement, but it has not been collected yet.

2. how the list is used

the entry at the building door is a controlled copy, and the studio coordinator is the person who can edit it. front-desk staff can check it when someone asks about entry, but they should not write additions on the paper copy or treat a verbal request as an approval. if a member finds an error, they can email the coordinator with the room and the hours they believe should appear. the coordinator then checks the request against the booking-period record and replies before making a change. a request that only concerns a room booking still goes to the front desk, not to the access-list process.

members may enter only during the hours written beside their names, and they must use their own key fob. sharing a fob, letting another person follow through the door, or propping the door open is not allowed under the studio’s existing entry rules. the update itself does not change those rules. when a class is taking place, a visiting tutor may be let in by the member hosting the class, but the tutor’s name is not added as a regular access entry on that basis. if the tutor needs independent access on another day, the coordinator needs a separate request and must check it before any list change.

there was one practical issue during the comparison: the print-room door reader did not accept two members’ fobs on march 9, even though both names were on the previous list. the maintenance desk reset those fobs the following morning. that report is recorded in the maintenance log, not in the access list, and there is no indication in the log that the list itself caused the reader problem. the coordinator checked the fobs again after the reset, but did not test entry to the recording room because neither member had permission for that room. anyone who has another failed entry should note the time and door and tell the front desk, so the report can be checked against the reader log.

the coordinator has asked staff to use the march 15 copy rather than the version dated january 6. copies kept in personal notebooks may not have been replaced, and the old sheet in the equipment cupboard is still awaiting collection. the cabinet copy and online staff-folder copy have the same names and hours as of march 15, but the online file is read-only for general staff. if a staff member spots a difference between those two copies, they should tell the coordinator rather than editing the online file or writing over the cabinet sheet.

the current assessment is that the access list matches the membership and access requests checked through march 12, for the two second-floor rooms and the north annex entrance list covered by this update. that assessment does not include room availability, future booking changes, or requests received after march 12. it also depends on the staff records being current; if a membership changes or a new access request is approved after this check, the coordinator will need to update the relevant entry. noa’s pending request and the uncollected older printout are still open items, and the march 15 copy should be treated as current only until another checked update replaces it.", "output": "The access list for the shared studio at North Annex has been updated for the spring booking period. This note explains what changed and what did not. It remains the working list for the two rooms on the second floor, the print room and the recording room. It is not an attendance record, and a name on the list does not mean that person has booked either room. The studio coordinator maintains the list, while the front desk keeps the booking calendar separately. This distinction matters because some people have been checking the access list to see whether a room is available, but that information is not included there. The current copy is in the cabinet beside the second-floor stairs, with a read-only copy in the online staff folder.

For this update, the coordinator compared the existing names with booking requests received by March 12 and staff records for current studio members. The comparison did not change anyone’s room booking, membership status, or key deposit. It was used only to determine who should remain on the access list for the spring period. The coordinator also checked each entry against contact details already on file, rather than asking members to provide new personal information. Where a record had an old email address, the list now shows the current address if it was already available in the staff record. The list does not show phone numbers, emergency contacts, or the reason a person needs access.

1. Changes to names and access

Mara Ellis and Jon Bell were added to the list because both have active memberships and submitted spring access requests. Mara can use the print room on weekdays from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m.; Jon can use the recording room on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. Their names are listed with those time limits, not with unrestricted access. Priya Shah remains listed for both rooms, with her existing weekday hours unchanged. She asked whether her Saturday workshop booking could be added too, but that booking appears on the calendar only and does not extend her regular access hours. The list continues to show weekday permission only for her.

Eli Turner’s entry was removed because his membership ended on February 28. This removal applies to both rooms and to the North Annex entrance list managed by the studio; it does not change the separate loan record for a microphone he returned last month. The coordinator has not yet received a completed spring request from Noa Kim, so Noa was not added in this update. If the request arrives, the coordinator will check it against the membership record before changing the list. Until then, Noa’s name is not on the current copy, although an older printout remains in the equipment cupboard. The older printout is marked for replacement, but has not yet been collected.

2. How the list is used

The entry at the building door is a controlled copy, and only the studio coordinator can edit it. Front-desk staff can check it when someone asks about entry, but they should not write additions on the paper copy or treat a verbal request as approval. If a member finds an error, they can email the coordinator with the room and hours they believe should appear. The coordinator then checks the request against the booking-period record and replies before making a change. A request that concerns only a room booking still goes to the front desk, not through the access-list process.

Members may enter only during the hours written beside their names, and they must use their own key fob. Sharing a fob, letting another person follow through the door, or propping the door open is not allowed under the studio’s existing entry rules. This update does not change those rules. When a class is taking place, a visiting tutor may be let in by the member hosting the class, but the tutor’s name is not added as a regular access entry on that basis. If the tutor needs independent access on another day, the coordinator needs a separate request and must check it before changing the list.

There was one practical issue during the comparison: the print-room door reader did not accept two members’ fobs on March 9, even though both names were on the previous list. The maintenance desk reset those fobs the following morning. That report is recorded in the maintenance log, not the access list, and the log does not indicate that the list itself caused the reader problem. The coordinator checked the fobs again after the reset, but did not test entry to the recording room because neither member had permission for that room. Anyone who has another failed entry should note the time and door and tell the front desk, so the report can be checked against the reader log.

The coordinator has asked staff to use the March 15 copy rather than the version dated January 6. Copies kept in personal notebooks may not have been replaced, and the old sheet in the equipment cupboard is still awaiting collection. The cabinet copy and online staff-folder copy have the same names and hours as of March 15, but the online file is read-only for general staff. If a staff member spots a difference between those copies, they should tell the coordinator rather than edit the online file or write over the cabinet sheet.

The current assessment is that the access list matches the membership and access requests checked through March 12, for the two second-floor rooms and the North Annex entrance list covered by this update. That assessment does not include room availability, future booking changes, or requests received after March 12. It also depends on the staff records being current; if a membership changes or a new access request is approved after this check, the coordinator will need to update the relevant entry. Noa’s pending request and the uncollected older printout remain open items, and the March 15 copy should be treated as current only until another checked update replaces it."}]
